notes:
Top-level summary: Mid-market SaaS (analytics product) evaluating Redwood to replace existing mix of self-hosted models + managed vector DB. Primary drivers: reduce ops cost, get consistent tail latency, and have audit logs + residency controls for customers.

Workload specifics / requirements (shorthand):
- Workload: semantic search + embeddings for product and support search, plus nightly batch re-index (~500k new/updated vectors per night).
- Throughput: target 150-250 qps for vector similarity queries during peak; 95th/99th tail latency goal <= 50ms for top-k responses (k=10) when served from cache/kv fast-path.
- Batch: ingest pipeline currently writes to Postgres + pgvector; prefer Redwood to integrate with same flow (we don't want new lock-in). Batch window 02:00-05:00 local — can tolerate some tail latency.
- Model preferences: prefer open models (Llama2/Mistral variants) quantized to 4-bit if quality holds; fallback plan: Redwood hosted for dev then Dedicated GPUs for production.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate-high. CFO asked for predictable monthly committed tiers (reserved capacity) vs variable hosted cost. Estimated ARR target with Redwood: $75k-$150k.
- Security/legal: SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS integration, retention policy controls, data residency (EU customers) — legal flagged retention >90 days for user-level logs.

Sales/eng notes (fragments):
- AE notes: "Likes the transparent perf numbers — wants raw p99 numbers vs marketing stats."
- CTO quote (paraphrase): "Need predictable monthly cost + SLA before we commit to Dedicated."
- SE notes: run perf harness against sample dataset (50M vectors) and real-world query distribution. Focus on hot-cache vs cold start for KV cache.
- Plan: proof-of-concept on Hosted API first (quick dev loop), then 30-day Dedicated trial for throughput validation + cost forecast.

Artifacts: Fireflies ff_session_2026-02-15-IRP-01, drive links above, Gmail thread for pricing. Jira REDW-1127 opened to track security docs request.
